submission.justification: Crystal-K3 gives the best 662 keV resolution (2.97% FWHM at 6 cm), but its background of 2.0 ± 0.2 counts/kg/day, from internal contamination, is about four times the facility budget of 0.5 counts/kg/day. It is therefore excluded for low-background operation, so the brief's goal of the best possible resolution cannot be met with K3. Among the admissible candidates, Crystal-K1 has the best resolution (4.496% FWHM at 6 cm in the simulation grid) and a background of 0.30 ± 0.05 counts/kg/day, which is within budget. Crystal-K2 has the lowest background (0.10) but roughly twice the FWHM (8.51%), so it is the fallback if background margin matters more than resolution. In the 2-10 cm grid, all three crystals reach their minimum FWHM at 6 cm. The 4 cm point for K1 (4.54%) is within the noise of single unrepeated runs. Caveats: the resolution values are simulated, not measured. The 2025 summary's claim of weak thickness dependence does not hold, since K1 at 8 cm is about 19% worse than at 6 cm. The K1 background margin is only 0.2 counts/kg/day, and the value is assumed independent of thickness. Thickness-dependent external background from the shielding was not modelled. Repeat runs at 4, 6 and 8 cm and a background check for the 6 cm geometry are recommended before final sign-off.
